attempts.summary: Built two independent transit networks between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) using their spare NICs (eth1/vtnet1 = 10.10.1.0/30, eth2/vtnet2 = 10.10.2.0/30), then used VyOS policy-based routing on node1 to steer node3->node4 traffic per destination TCP port: dport 8080 is fwmarked and routed via table 101 (transit1/eth1), dport 9090 via table 102 (transit2/eth2). node3 redirects node4-bound 8080/9090 traffic to node1 via a marked policy route/table (systemd-persisted). node2 forwards the marked traffic onward to node4 over its LAN interface (vtnet0), with pf pass rules added for the two new OPT interfaces. Opened node4's firewalld for port 8080 (9090 was already permitted) so both flows complete. Verified via tcpdump on node1's eth1/eth2 that port 8080 traffic exclusively traverses transit1 and port 9090 traffic exclusively traverses transit2, both delivering full TCP payloads to node4. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes (node3, node4, node1, node2), confirming changed boot identity on each (boot_id for Linux nodes, kern.boottime for FreeBSD node2) and re-verifying full recovery of transit connectivity, PBR routing tables/marks, pf rules, firewalld config, and successful port-differentiated end-to-end delivery after each restart.
